comments.body:
## Phase 1 evidence capture (AC1) — first-hand read-only CloudWatch + in-repo/runtime evidence

Debug worktree `debug/3a52-root-disk-pressure` off `origin/main` (0b851c8103). All AWS calls
below are read-only `cloudwatch:GetMetricStatistics` / `ListMetrics`. **No host access was
used** — `ssm:SendCommand` is blocked in this session, so journald/`du` evidence is NOT part
of this record (see "What still needs a host operation" at the end).

### 1. The reclaim is not a prune — it is a return to a FIXED floor

`rebar/host:root_disk_used_percent`, 5-min samples, 2026-08-15 → 2026-08-19: **23 drops of
≥5 percentage points, and every one lands on 48%** (two on 49%/51%). Drop sizes range
1.5 GiB → 12.6 GiB. The incident drop is `90% @22:00 → 48% @22:05` = 12.6 GiB.

A `docker builder prune --keep-storage 5GB` + `docker image prune -f` leaves a *variable*
residue that depends on what was reclaimable at that moment. It cannot produce an identical
48% floor across 23 independent events of wildly different sizes. A constant floor is the
signature of an **ephemeral working set being destroyed wholesale**, returning the disk to
its baseline.

### 2. Growth tracks REVIEW volume, not deploy volume

`review_bot_llm_total_tokens` was sustained 0.8M–3.0M per 5 min from 20:35 straight through
22:30 — reviews ran continuously *before, during and after* the drop. Root-disk growth rate
was ~4.4 GiB/h **before** the drop (69%→90% over 85 min) and ~4.3 GiB/h **after** it
(48%→54% over 25 min). Same rate, same driver, uninterrupted by the reclaim.

### 3. The deferral episode did not cover the growth window

`deploy_deferrals`: **0** in every 5-min bucket from 20:30 through 21:50, then 2 / 3 / 1 at
21:55 / 22:00 / 22:05. The disk crossed `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT` (80%) at **21:25** and the 85%
alarm floor at **21:35** — 20–30 minutes *before* the first deferral. So the deferral path
cannot be what suppressed reclaim during the climb, and `deploy_errors` = `voter_errors` =
`review_interrupts` = **0** throughout (no backoff, no failed deploy, no ENOSPC).

### 4. Both docker-prune hypotheses are therefore weakened, and the disk-consumer question moves

`infra/scripts/docker-compose.yml`'s `review-bot` service mounts **only**
`./rebar-bot-signing-key` (ro), `gerrit_reviewbot` → `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot`, and
`gerrit_reviewbot_tickets` → `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets` — both bind-backed onto the
**separate 50-GiB `/var/gerrit` EBS volume**. There is no `tmpfs` and no other mount, and
`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` is not set in the compose environment. So everything else the bot writes
at runtime lands on the **container writable layer**, i.e. `/var/lib/docker` on the 30-GiB
**root** volume — and those bytes are neither buildkit cache nor a dangling image, so
`prune_docker_caches` **cannot reclaim them at all** while the container is running.

`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:113` `store_root()` =
`config.resolve_gate_tmpdir() or tempfile.gettempdir()` + store dirname. Verified at runtime
with `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` unset: it resolves under `tempfile.gettempdir()`, i.e. `/tmp` inside
the container.

### 5. RUNTIME EXPERIMENT (AC2 discriminator, part 1): the snapshot janitor cannot fire before the alarm

Drove the **real** `rebar._snapshot.janitor.run_gc()` with injected free-space values for a
30-GiB root (5 warm, out-of-grace, not-cold entries — the bot's steady state under continuous
review load):

| root used | free injected | evicted | reclaimed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 71% (pre-incident) | 8.70 GiB | **0** | 0 |
| 80% (`DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`) | 6.00 GiB | **0** | 0 |
| **85% (CloudWatch ALARM floor)** | 4.50 GiB | **0** | 0 |
| **90% (observed incident peak)** | 3.00 GiB | **0** | 0 |
| 94% (past the watermark) | 1.80 GiB | 5 | 20480 |

`src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:53` `DEFAULT_FREE_WATERMARK_BYTES = 2 * 1024**3`. On a 30-GiB
root that watermark is only crossed at **93.3% used** — strictly *above* the 85% alarm floor
and above the 90% peak actually reached. **The alarm necessarily fires before snapshot GC can
ever engage.** This is hypothesis 1 of the ticket, now confirmed dynamically rather than by
reading the constant.

### 6. The health dip is the same event, caught by sampling luck

`reviewbot_healthy` (dimension `InstanceId=i-00880b2c7f13527c5`) was 0 in exactly **two**
5-min buckets across 2026-08-15→19; one of them is **2026-08-17 22:05** — the same bucket as
the 90%→48% drop. Only 1 of the 23 reclaim events shows a health dip because the host probe
polls every 5 minutes and the recreation window is seconds long. No separate cause is needed
for the "review-bot drops unhealthy" symptom.

### Working account (not yet fully proven)

One mechanism explains every symptom: the review-bot's **ephemeral per-review working set**
lives on the container writable layer (30-GiB root) because no volume covers it; it is
invisible to `prune_docker_caches`; the snapshot janitor's 2-GiB-free watermark sits below the
alarm floor so GC never engages; and the bytes are freed only when a deploy **recreates** the
container — hence the constant 48% floor and the coincident health dip.

### What still needs a host operation (blocked here)

`ssm:SendCommand` is denied in this session, so I could not run the bounded read-only host
probe that would name the **dominant** consumer directly. The exact command wanted is a
read-only `AWS-RunShellScript` on `i-00880b2c7f13527c5`:
`df -h /`; `docker system df -v`; `docker ps --size`; `du -xh --max-depth=2 /tmp` **inside the
review-bot container**; and
`journalctl -u rebar-autodeploy.service --since "2026-08-18 03:30" --until "2026-08-18 06:00"`
plus a count of `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` markers (that marker is deliberately not published
as a CloudWatch metric — story 28f9 scoped it out — so journald is its only reader).
`docker ps --size` alone would settle it: it prints each running container's writable-layer
size.

rebar-debug Phase 1, Stage 3 continues; no repair has been attempted.

## AC2 discriminating experiment — the Docker-cache hypothesis is FALSIFIED

Two rival consumers were live. This experiment separates them on a prediction they
disagree about, using only read-only CloudWatch and local `git`.

**Rival A** (ticket hypothesis 2, "autodeploy prunes Docker caches too late"): the bytes are
buildkit cache + image layers from review-bot rebuilds. Build artifacts can only be created
by a **build**, and autodeploy only builds when `main` advances with a `BOT_PATHS`/
`SECRETS_PATHS` change. → **Predicts: in a window with no such commit, the root disk is flat.**

**Rival B**: the bytes are the review-bot's ephemeral per-review working set on the
container's writable layer. → **Predicts: the disk grows at the same rate in build-free
windows, as long as reviews are running.**

Method: cut the 5-min `root_disk_used_percent` series at every `origin/main` commit touching
`BOT_PATHS`/`SECRETS_PATHS`, allow 15 min after each for autodeploy to notice + build +
prune, and measure growth inside each maximal build-free interval ≥40 min. Intervals
containing a reclaim were excluded so a drop cannot confound the rate. 1 pt = 0.30 GiB.

| build-free interval (UTC) | mins | Δ% | GiB/h | LLM tokens |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 08-16 23:46 → 08-17 17:18 | 1052 | +34 | **+0.59** | 23.2M |
| 08-17 17:33 → 08-17 20:14 | 161 | +23 | **+2.67** | 8.7M |
| 08-17 20:29 → 08-18 04:16 | 467 | +29 | **+1.12** | 20.8M |
| 08-18 05:13 → 08-18 07:02 | 110 | +17 | **+2.91** | 14.1M |
| 08-18 10:00 → 08-18 11:13 | 73 | +3 | +0.83 | 5.0M |
| 08-18 11:28 → 08-18 13:07 | 100 | +5 | +0.95 | 1.3M |
| 08-18 18:15 → 08-18 22:03 | 227 | +31 | **+2.54** | 11.2M |
| 08-18 22:43 → 08-18 23:51 | 68 | +9 | **+2.49** | 7.8M |
| 08-19 03:22 → 08-19 04:26 | 64 | +1 | +0.33 | 4.6M |
| 08-19 06:39 → 08-19 07:36 | 57 | +12 | **+3.93** | 2.2M |
| 08-19 10:39 → 08-19 12:15 | 96 | +3 | +0.57 | 3.4M |
| 08-19 13:44 → 08-19 14:56 | 72 | +0 | **+0.00** | 0.6M |

n=12; growth GiB/h min +0.00, median **+1.12**, max **+3.93**. **10 of 12 build-free
intervals grew faster than 0.5 GiB/h**, and the single interval that did **not** grow at all
is the one with almost no review activity (0.6M tokens).

**Result: Rival A is rejected.** Buildkit cache and image layers cannot appear without a
build, yet the disk climbs at up to 3.93 GiB/h across windows in which no rebuild was
possible. The one flat interval is flat because *reviews* stopped, not because *builds*
stopped. Rival B's prediction holds.

Corroborating (E3): all **23** reclaim events over 2026-08-15→19 are preceded by a
`BOT_PATHS` commit (22/23 within 60 min, 16/23 within 30 min); there is no reclaim in any
build-free window. Reclamation is tied to the deploy, not to the pressure gate.

### Where the growing bytes must be

`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:223-240` — the `review-bot` service's only mounts are
`./rebar-bot-signing-key` (ro), `gerrit_reviewbot` → `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot`, and
`gerrit_reviewbot_tickets` → `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets`; both named volumes are
bind-backed onto the **separate 50-GiB `/var/gerrit` EBS volume**. No `tmpfs`, no other mount.
So every other runtime write lands on the container's writable layer = `/var/lib/docker` on
the **30-GiB root**.

`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` is set **nowhere** — not in `docker-compose.yml`'s environment block, not
in `infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh` (which generates the SSM-sourced `.env`), not in
`infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot`. So `store_root()`
(`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:113`) provably falls through to
`tempfile.gettempdir()` → **`/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots` inside the container**, on the root
disk. That is the same path the alarm's own description already names as a root-disk reclaim
target (`infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:213`).

Those bytes belong to a **running** container's read-write layer: they are neither buildkit
cache (`docker builder prune`) nor a dangling image (`docker image prune`), so
`prune_docker_caches` cannot reclaim them **at all** — which is why the reclaim gate story
28f9 added could not have prevented this breach no matter when it fired.

comments.body:
# Phase 1 EXIT — confirmed root cause (rebar-debug)

Two causes, and two are needed: one explains the **growth rate**, the other explains the
**failure to reclaim**. Neither alone explains both symptoms.

---

## RC-A (why there was so much to reclaim) — every review writes a full ~620 MiB / ~70,000-file copy of the ticket store, keyed on a ref that advances every ~26 seconds, and nothing ever frees it

`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:99` calls `materialize_tickets(...)` on every attested gate
resolution. `materialize_tickets` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:675-703`)
content-addresses the entry as `<store>/tickets-<sha>` and builds it via `_materialize_tree`
(`:373-410`, `git read-tree` + `git checkout-index`) — every file written fresh, no
hardlinking, no delta, no per-review release (`SnapshotHandle._cleanup` at `:199` is never
assigned by any producer). `_pin_tickets_sha` (`:534-609`) pins the **live** tracker HEAD via
`config.tracker_dir()`, and `tracker_dir_override()` (`src/rebar/_config_sources.py:65-79`)
returns the container's `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` verbatim, so the key is the tickets branch tip.

Measured independently on this checkout:

- tickets tree = **69,984 blobs** (≈620 MiB; ~800 MiB allocated). Code snapshot for comparison:
  41.6 MiB / 3,131 files — **15× smaller**.
- **1,374 commits** on `origin/tickets` in the 10-hour incident window — HEAD moves every ~26 s.
- each of the last 5 consecutive tickets commits changed **exactly 1 file**.

So a ~1-file delta produces a fresh 620 MiB copy: ~10^5× write amplification, on a key with
effectively **zero reuse**. At ~0.85 GiB per review (tickets + code entry) and the observed
review cadence this models **2.5-10 GiB/h**; measured growth was **4.4 GiB/h**. Match.

The review-bot's own `code_review` artifact write (`REBAR_SYNC_PUSH: always`,
`docker-compose.yml:120`) guarantees the ref advances between reviews even if nothing else in
the fleet were writing.

## RC-B (why nothing reclaimed it before the alarm) — both janitor eviction triggers are structurally unreachable in this deployment, and the third one the ADR promises was never implemented

`_gc_pass` (`src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:303-345`) has exactly two eviction predicates:

- **`need_space = free < cfg.free_watermark_bytes`** (`janitor.py:318`), default **2 GiB**
  (`janitor.py:53`). That is an **absolute** floor and it is disk-size-blind. On a 30-GiB root
  it is crossed only at **93.3% used** — above the `rebar-root-disk-pressure` threshold of
  **85%** (`infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:226`) and above the observed **90%** peak.
- **`too_cold = mtime < now - max_age_seconds`**, default **7 days** (`janitor.py:55`). The
  store lives on a writable layer destroyed on every redeploy — 23 reclaim events in 4 days,
  i.e. a container lifetime of hours. **No entry can ever reach 7 days**; the cold-trim is dead
  code here.
- The third trigger, promised by `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md:72-73` and by
  the module's own contract docstring (`janitor.py:13-15`) — "backstopped by the
  incrementally-maintained byte total" — **does not exist**: `_gc_pass` reads only `free` and
  `mtime`. The only reader of `byte_total` is `startup_sweep` (`janitor.py:251`), for
  reconciliation. There is no store-size cap knob at all (`docs/config.md:474-484`).
- Compounding it: `materialize_tickets` bypasses `cache.acquire` and so **never calls
  `add_bytes`** — even if the ADR's backstop existed it would under-count the dominant consumer
  to **zero**.

The janitor **is** started (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:134-136`) and ran every 300 s
throughout the incident. It correctly evicted nothing. "GC never ran" is falsified.

---

## Proof — discriminating experiments

**E1 (runtime, decisive for RC-B).** Drove the real `rebar._snapshot.janitor.run_gc()` with
injected free-space values for a 30-GiB root against 5 warm, out-of-grace, not-cold entries:

| root used | free injected | evicted |
|---|---|---|
| 80% (`DISK_PRESSURE_PCT`) | 6.00 GiB | **0** |
| **85% (CloudWatch ALARM floor)** | 4.50 GiB | **0** |
| **90% (observed incident peak)** | 3.00 GiB | **0** |
| 94% (past the watermark) | 1.80 GiB | 5 |

Provably inert across the entire range the incident occupied. A `dynamic` claim confirmed by
execution, not by reading the constant.

**E5 (falsifies the Docker-cache rival).** Buildkit cache and image layers cannot exist without
a build, and autodeploy only builds when `main` advances with a `BOT_PATHS`/`SECRETS_PATHS`
change. Cutting the `root_disk_used_percent` series at every such commit (+15 min for
build/prune, excluding intervals containing a reclaim) yields 12 maximal build-free intervals:
**10 of 12 grew faster than 0.5 GiB/h; median +1.12, max +3.93 GiB/h — with no rebuild
possible.** The single non-growing interval (+0.00) is the one where *review* activity nearly
stopped (0.6M LLM tokens). Growth tracks reviews, not builds. **Ticket hypothesis 2 (Docker
prune timing) is rejected.**

Three further nails in that rival: (i) the largest reclaim, **12.6 GiB**, exceeds the entire
5 GB buildkit ceiling plus any plausible dangling-image set; (ii) `--keep-storage` leaves a
*variable* LRU residue, so 23 independent prunes cannot converge on an identical floor, whereas
destroying a container writable layer converges **by construction** — and 23 of 23 drops land
on **48%**; (iii) with `deploy_deferrals = 0` for every bucket 20:30-21:50, the `TARGET ==
DEPLOYED` no-op branch *was* being taken, so from 21:25 (80%) a pressure prune fired roughly
every 10 min — and the disk climbed **80% → 90% straight through them**.

**E3.** All 23 reclaim events over 2026-08-15→19 are preceded by a `BOT_PATHS` commit (22/23
within 60 min); no reclaim occurs in any build-free window. Reclamation is tied to container
recreation, never to the pressure gate.

**E4.** `deploy_deferrals` was 0 through 21:50; the disk crossed 80% at 21:25 and 85% at 21:35,
**20-30 min before the first deferral**. The drain gate is a bystander that delayed the
recreation which would otherwise have reset the disk sooner — an aggravating factor, not the
cause. `deploy_errors` = `voter_errors` = `review_interrupts` = 0 throughout.

**E2.** With `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` unset, `store_root()` resolves under `tempfile.gettempdir()`.
`REBAR_GATE_*` appears **nowhere** in `docker-compose.yml`, `Dockerfile.reviewbot`, or
`fetch-secrets.sh`, and the `review-bot` service's only mounts are `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot`
and `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets` (bind-backed onto the separate 50-GiB EBS volume) plus
a read-only key file — no `tmpfs`. So `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots` is on the container's
**writable layer**, on the 30-GiB root.

**Ruled out as the leak:** the per-change clone workdir
(`src/rebar/review_bot/voter.py:572`, `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory` in a `with` block —
released on every exit path); the LLM-workflow run snapshot (`llm/workflow/snapshot.py:70-74`,
rooted at that temp clone and capped at 512 MiB, `:43`); journald (survives container
recreation, so it cannot produce a constant floor).

---

## Every symptom accounted for

| symptom | cause |
|---|---|
| root disk 71% → 90% in ~1 h at 4.4 GiB/h | RC-A: ~0.85 GiB of fresh snapshot per review |
| the alarm breached 85% and kept climbing | RC-B: the only bounding mechanism cannot engage until 93.3% |
| abrupt 90% → **48%** at 22:05 | deploy recreated the container; the writable layer (store included) destroyed |
| **all 23** drops land on the identical 48% | wholesale destruction of an ephemeral layer, not a variable-residue prune |
| `reviewbot_healthy` = 0 in the 22:05 bucket only | the 5-min host probe sampled during that recreation; 1-of-23 is the expected hit rate for a seconds-long window |
| `voter_errors` = 0 | never reached ENOSPC — recreation came before exhaustion |
| `deploy_deferrals` 2/3/1 at 21:55-22:05 | the drain gate delayed the recreation, so this episode reached 90% instead of resetting earlier |
| story 28f9's mitigation did not prevent it | `prune_docker_caches` cannot reclaim a **running** container's writable layer, whenever it fires |

No residual symptom is unexplained.

---

## Defect legitimacy

**RC-B — `defect` / `incomplete-implementation`.** Cited authorities, all violated:

- `infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:500-508` — the documented defense ordering: the janitor
  "reclaims `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots` on a free-space watermark", and the alarm pages "so
  exhaustion is caught **before** it silently fail-closes the gate." In practice the ordering is
  inverted: the backstop fires and the primary never does.
- `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md:72-73` and `janitor.py:13-15` — both specify a
  byte-total backstop that `_gc_pass` does not implement (`incomplete-implementation`).
- `infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:209-215, 226` — the alarm contract names 85% as the
  actionable threshold and `/tmp/rebar-gate-snapshots` as a reclaim target for it.
- Prior **closed** bug `7a41-95f4-c38c-4b5a` AC2 — "a disk-headroom check … so exhaustion is
  caught **before** it vetoes reviews." A previously-fixed behaviour class.
- This ticket's own AC4.

Not `environment-or-config`: an operator *can* set `REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_BYTES`, but the
shipped **default** is what is wrong, and an absolute byte floor is disk-size-blind by
construction — no single absolute value is correct across hosts.

**RC-A — `defect`.** `docs/adr/0005-snapshot-cache-architecture.md` D2 rests on "an immutable
SHA is a perfect cache key", which holds only for keys with **reuse**. The tickets ref has
none — it advances every ~26 s — so the structure is not a cache but an append-only log of
620-MiB full copies, contradicting the ADR's own claim that the store is bounded and
reclaimable.

---

## What was NOT established

`ssm:SendCommand` is blocked in this session, so there is **no** host `du` / `docker system df`
/ journald evidence in this record. RC-A's dominance rests on measured artifact sizes, measured
ref churn, the code path, and the rate match — not on a direct measurement of the live
directory. The one host operation still wanted, purely read-only:
`docker ps --size` and `du -xh --max-depth=1 /tmp` inside `compose-review-bot-1`. It would
confirm the split rather than change the conclusion.

Phase 1 complete. Siblings filed for the two causes that are out of this ticket's repair scope.

comments.body:
# rebar-debug final report

## Problem

`rebar-root-disk-pressure` breached on the `rebar-gerrit` host: the 30-GiB root volume climbed
71% → 90% over ~an hour on 2026-08-17, the alarm fired at 21:51 PDT, `reviewbot_healthy` dipped
to 0 at 22:05, and the disk then dropped abruptly to 48%. Story `sour-plugugly-rhino`'s
pressure-triggered Docker prune had not prevented it.

## Proven root cause

Two causes; both are needed, because one explains the **growth rate** and the other the
**failure to reclaim**.

**RC-B (repaired here) — the snapshot janitor's reclaim triggers are structurally unreachable
on this volume.** `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:53`
`DEFAULT_FREE_WATERMARK_BYTES = 2 * 1024**3` is an **absolute**, disk-size-blind floor. On a
30-GiB root it is crossed only at **93.3% used** — above the 85% alarm
(`infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:226`) and above the 90% peak actually reached. The
7-day cold-trim (`janitor.py:55`) exceeds the container's lifetime (23 recreations in 4 days),
and the byte-total backstop that ADR 0005 and the module docstring both promise is not
implemented in `_gc_pass`. The janitor **is** started
(`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:134-136`) and ran every 300 s throughout — it correctly evicted
nothing.

**RC-A (split to `smart-disloyal-naga`) — the growth source.** Every review materializes a full
~620 MiB / 69,984-file copy of the ticket tree (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:99` →
`_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:675-703`, `git read-tree` + `checkout-index`, no hardlinks, no
delta, no release), keyed on the tickets tip — which advanced **1,374 times** in the 10-hour
incident window, with consecutive commits differing by **exactly 1 file**. ~0.85 GiB per review
models 2.5-10 GiB/h against the measured 4.4 GiB/h.

The store is on the root disk because `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` is set **nowhere**
(`docker-compose.yml`, `Dockerfile.reviewbot`, `fetch-secrets.sh`), so `store_root()`
(`repo_snapshot.py:113`) falls through to `tempfile.gettempdir()` — the container's writable
layer, which no volume mount covers.

## Proof

- **E1 (runtime, decisive).** Drove the real `run_gc()` with injected free space on a 30-GiB
  volume: **0 evictions at 4.50 GiB free (85% used) and at 3.00 GiB free (90% used)**; first
  eviction only past 93.3%.
- **E5 (falsifies the rival).** Ticket hypothesis 2 said the bytes were buildkit cache/images
  from autodeploy rebuilds. Build artifacts cannot exist without a build. Across 12 maximal
  build-free intervals, **10 grew faster than 0.5 GiB/h (median +1.12, max +3.93)**, and the
  only flat one (+0.00) is where *review* activity nearly stopped. **Rejected.**
- Three further nails: the 12.6-GiB reclaim exceeds the whole 5 GB buildkit ceiling;
  `--keep-storage` leaves a variable residue so 23 prunes cannot converge on the identical
  **48%** floor observed; and with `deploy_deferrals = 0` from 20:30-21:50 the no-op branch
  *was* being taken, so a pressure prune fired ~every 10 min from 21:25 while the disk climbed
  80% → 90% straight through them.
- **E3/E4.** All 23 reclaims follow a `BOT_PATHS` commit; none occurs in a build-free window.
  Deferrals began 20-30 min *after* the alarm floor was crossed, so the drain gate is an
  aggravating bystander, not the cause.

## Test

`tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py` — 7 new cases. Observed **RED on the assertions** (not on
a construction error: a field-only scaffold was used to prove the failure reason), e.g.
*"at 85% used on a 30-GiB volume the janitor must reclaim BEFORE the rebar-root-disk-pressure
alarm fires, not after"*. The file was moved out of the fixer's tree entirely — the
implementation was written against a frozen contract card only. It then went **GREEN (24/24)**
against that held-out oracle, and the **exact-defect mutation** (forcing `_space_thresholds`
back to the absolute-only watermark) returned the same 4 cases to RED. The assertions are on
`GcResult.evicted` / `skipped_grace` / entry existence — observable output of the public
`run_gc` API, so they are not change-detectors.

## Fix

Add a second, **volume-relative** term to the janitor's free-space trigger. The trigger is the
**larger** of the absolute floor and `free_watermark_pct` percent of the volume, so raising one
term can never weaken the other; once a pass starts it runs on to a target
`RECLAIM_TARGET_MARGIN_PCT` (5) points higher — a fixed internal constant, deliberately not an
operator knob — so it overshoots the threshold rather than stalling on it and re-firing every
interval. The percentage is **whole integer points**, matching the janitor's existing int-only
config seam; a fractional value would be truncated to 0 by `_snapshot_int` and silently disable
the term (this was caught by the plan-review gate before implementation). It defaults to **0
(off)**, so every existing deployment is bit-identical; the review-bot service opts in at
**20** (reclaim at 80% used), matching `autodeploy.sh`'s `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT=80`.

This addresses the mechanism, not the symptom: it makes the documented ordering
(`infra/runbooks/review-bot-ops.md:500-508` — the janitor reclaims, the alarm is the backstop)
actually hold on a small volume.

Files: `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py`, `src/rebar/_config_sources.py`,
`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, `docs/config.md`, `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`,
`docs/env-vars.md`, `tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py`.

## Scope & safety

- **Caller-dependency sweep:** `run_gc`/`_gc_pass`'s only behavioural consumer is the
  review-bot lifespan via `start_background_janitor()` → `JanitorConfig.from_env()`. With the
  new knob defaulting to 0 its behaviour is unchanged unless the env var is set — **incidental
  usage only**, no behavioural dependency broken.
- **Restoration, not creation:** no new entry point, command, or user-visible artifact; it
  restores an ordering the runbook already specifies.
- **No new dependency.**
- **No test weakened.** `_snapshot_int` was refactored (its last parameter became the defaults
  mapping, indexed by the key it already used) purely to keep `_config_sources.py` under the
  repo's 800-line hard cap after adding the entry — behaviour-preserving, and the helper is
  private with no callers outside its module. `_reverify_pass` was extracted verbatim from
  `_gc_pass` to stay under the complexity ceiling.
- Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck` (567 files), `check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
  (`new=0 increased=0`), module sizes 432 / 791 — all green.

## Siblings

- **Construct sweep:** the construct is "an absolute byte threshold compared against free disk
  space". `shutil.disk_usage` / `statvfs` appear **nowhere else** in `src/` — no siblings.
- **Parity sweep:** the rule is "a reclaim threshold must sit below the operator's alarm floor".
  Surfaces: the snapshot janitor (**fixed**); `autodeploy.sh`'s `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT=80`
  (**already correct**, below 85%); the 50-GiB `/var/gerrit` data volume, alarmed at 85% by
  `rebar-gerrit-data-disk-high` but with **no reclaim surface at all** — **accepted**, with the
  rationale already documented at `docker-compose.yml:210-216` (append-only `usage.jsonl` at
  ~100-200 MB/year against 44 GiB free). Note this becomes load-bearing if anyone "fixes" the
  root-disk problem by relocating the snapshot store onto `/var/gerrit`: that converts a
  root-disk incident into a data-disk one, which would take Gerrit itself down.

## Residual risk & prevention

- **`smart-disloyal-naga`** (ticket filed) — RC-A: the ~620 MiB-per-review ticket-tree copy on
  a cache key with no reuse. Unbounded by construction; this fix bounds the *store*, not the
  *rate*.
- **`itchy-arbored-peccary`** (ticket filed) — the ADR-promised byte-total backstop is absent
  from `_gc_pass`, and `materialize_tickets` never calls `add_bytes`, so the dominant entries
  are byte-accounted at zero. Also the prerequisite for defaulting `free_watermark_pct` on
  everywhere (Option B in the plan) rather than opting in per deployment.
- **`uninspired-gabardine-pilchard`** (ticket filed) — `AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE` is emitted as
  a journal marker but published as no metric (story 28f9 scoped it out), so "did the reclaim
  gate run?" is answerable only with host access. This directly lengthened this investigation.
- **Accepted:** the 7-day cold-trim is dead code on a container recreated hourly. Harmless
  here, but it means the space watermark is the *only* live trigger — which is precisely what
  made this incident possible.

## Replication

Re-ran the incident's CloudWatch series through the real janitor using the **deployed
configuration path** (`JanitorConfig.from_env()` with `REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT=20`, as
compose now sets it) on a 30-GiB volume. Reclamation now engages at the **82%** sample —
**below the 85% alarm floor** — where pre-fix every sample from 69% through 90% reclaimed
nothing. The original report no longer reproduces.

## Not established (host access blocked)

`ssm:SendCommand` is denied in this session, so no host `du` / `docker system df` / journald
evidence is in this record. RC-A's dominance rests on measured artifact sizes, measured ref
churn, the code path, and the rate match rather than a direct measurement of the live
directory. The one read-only host command still wanted: `docker ps --size` plus
`du -xh --max-depth=1 /tmp` inside `compose-review-bot-1`. It would confirm the split, not
change the conclusion.

comments.body:
## Patchset 2 — review-driven hardening of the new knob

Code review on patchset 1 returned `LLM-Review +1` with three advisory findings. One is a genuine footgun in the knob this change introduces, so patchset 2 acts on it rather than resolving it away.

**`free_watermark_pct` had no upper bound.** It is headroom to *keep free*, but `80` reads naturally as "reclaim at 80% used" — the inverse. Reproduced on a 30-GiB volume:

| pct | trigger | | 
|---|---|---|
| 20 | 6.00 GiB free | intended |
| 80 | 24.00 GiB free | `free < trigger` true at every plausible level |
| 100 | 30.00 GiB free | **trigger >= the whole volume** |

At 80 or above every pass evicts the entire store and every gate re-materializes its snapshot from scratch; at >=100 the trigger exceeds the volume outright. Since the docs added by this same change tell operators to set the knob, shipping that range would introduce a new defect. Patchset 2 clamps to `MAX_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT = 50` — clamped rather than rejected, because a janitor must never fail a gate over a tunable.

Verified RED first (`AssertionError: the trigger must never demand the whole volume be free`), then GREEN. A second new test covers the reviewer's third finding — that `max()` was only exercised in the direction where the volume-relative term dominates; on a 10-GiB volume with `pct=10` the 2-GiB absolute floor correctly wins. That one passed unchanged, so it was a coverage gap, not a bug.

The second finding (`_snapshot_int` can now `KeyError` on a defaults mapping missing the key) is left as-is: the helper is private to `_config_sources.py`, its only caller passes the complete mapping built by `_default_tunables()`, and a missing key there is a programming error that should fail loudly rather than silently resolve to a wrong default.

Re-verified on patchset 2: 26/26 in `tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py`, the exact-defect mutation still returns the original four cases to RED, the incident replay still reclaims at 82% (below the 85% floor), `make lint` + `make typecheck` green, complexity ratchet `new=0 increased=0`, and the full `tests/unit` suite passed locally on patchset 1's tree.

Note: the amend regenerated the `Change-Id` and briefly opened a duplicate (change 1923). The original id was restored so this is **patchset 2 of [change 1922](https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1922)**, and 1923 is abandoned. The stale `LLM-Review +1` was dropped by the new patchset, as expected; both gates are re-running.

compiled_state.description:
## Context

`rebar-root-disk-pressure` went ALARM 2026-08-17 21:51 PDT (OK 22:12) on `rebar-gerrit`
(`i-00880b2c7f13527c5`, 30-GiB gp3 root). Root usage climbed 71% @20:55 → 90% @21:55/22:00,
then dropped to 48% @22:05; `reviewbot_healthy` dipped to 0 at 22:05.

## Phase 1: COMPLETE — root cause proven

Full evidence in the "Phase 1 EXIT" comment (experiments, CloudWatch series, citations).
Summary:

- **REJECTED — "autodeploy prunes Docker caches too late."** Build artifacts cannot appear
  without a build; 10 of 12 build-free intervals still grew (median +1.12, max +3.93 GiB/h).
  The 12.6-GiB reclaim exceeds the whole 5 GB buildkit ceiling. `prune_docker_caches` cannot
  reclaim a **running** container's writable layer at all.
- **CONFIRMED (RC-B, this ticket) — the janitor's reclaim triggers are unreachable here.**
  `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:53` `DEFAULT_FREE_WATERMARK_BYTES = 2 GiB` is an **absolute**,
  disk-size-blind floor: on a 30-GiB root it is crossed only at **93.3% used**, above the 85%
  alarm (`infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:226`) and above the 90% peak reached.
  Driving the real `run_gc()` with injected free space gives **0 evictions at 85% and at 90%
  used**; first eviction only past 93.3%. The 7-day cold-trim (`janitor.py:55`) exceeds the
  container's lifetime (23 recreations in 4 days). The janitor *is* started
  (`src/rebar/review_bot/app.py:134-136`) and correctly evicted nothing.
- **CONFIRMED (RC-A, split to `smart-disloyal-naga`) — the growth source.** Every review
  materializes a full ~620 MiB / 69,984-file copy of the ticket tree
  (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:99` → `_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:675-703`), keyed on a tip
  that advanced 1,374 times in the 10-hour window with consecutive commits differing by 1 file.

The store sits on the 30-GiB root because `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` is unset everywhere, so
`store_root()` (`repo_snapshot.py:113`) falls through to `tempfile.gettempdir()` = the
container writable layer. The 48% floor and the 22:05 health dip are one event: the deploy
recreating the container and destroying that layer.

## Scope of THIS ticket

RC-B only — make reclaim engage **before** the alarm floor. RC-A is `smart-disloyal-naga`; the
missing byte-total backstop and `add_bytes` accounting are `itchy-arbored-peccary`.

## Plan

Add a **volume-relative** headroom term to the janitor's free-space trigger so the watermark
cannot sit above the alarm floor on a small volume, plus hysteresis so a pass reclaims past the
trigger instead of re-firing every 300 s. Both new values are **integers** so they survive the
existing int-only config seam (`_snapshot_int` coerces with `int()`, and `JanitorConfig`'s
fields and `_default_tunables()` are `dict[str, int]`) — a float fraction would truncate to 0
and silently disable the fix.

1. `src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py` — add `DEFAULT_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT = 0` and
   `free_watermark_pct: int` (whole percent of the volume; `0` = relative term off) to
   `JanitorConfig` + `_default_tunables()`. Add a module-level
   `RECLAIM_TARGET_MARGIN_PCT = 5` constant — a fixed internal margin, not an operator knob,
   matching how `DEFAULT_GRACE_SECONDS` / `DEFAULT_INTERVAL_SECONDS` are handled. In
   `_gc_pass`, take `total = shutil.disk_usage(root).total` and compute:
   - `trigger = max(free_watermark_bytes, total * free_watermark_pct // 100)`
   - `target  = max(free_watermark_bytes, total * (free_watermark_pct + RECLAIM_TARGET_MARGIN_PCT) // 100)`

   Evict when `free < trigger`, and once triggered keep evicting until `free >= target`. The
   grace window and `_is_entry`'s `tickets-` recognition are untouched.

   Worked example, 30-GiB root, `free_watermark_pct = 20`: `trigger` = 6.0 GiB free (80% used),
   `target` = 7.5 GiB free (75% used). Both sit below the 85% alarm floor (4.5 GiB free), which
   is what AC4 requires. With `free_watermark_pct = 0` the arithmetic collapses to
   `max(2 GiB, 0)` = today's behaviour exactly.

2. `src/rebar/_config_sources.py` — resolve `free_watermark_pct` through the existing
   `resolve_janitor_tunables` int path (`REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT` > `[snapshot]` table >
   default `0`). No new float helper is needed.
3. `infra/compose/docker-compose.yml` — set `REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT: "20"` on the
   `review-bot` service, the pattern already used for `REBAR_TRACKER_DIR` and
   `REBAR_USAGE_LOG`. 20 is `autodeploy.sh:110`'s `DISK_PRESSURE_PCT=80` expressed as headroom,
   chosen there as below the 85% alarm for hysteresis.
4. `docs/config.md`, `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`, `docs/env-vars.md` — document the one new
   knob and the fixed margin.
5. `tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py` — the RED oracle.

### Design decision for review: what should `free_watermark_pct` default to?

- **Option A (this plan) — default `0` (off), set to `20` for the review-bot host in compose.**
  No behaviour change for any existing rebar user; fixes this host. Cost: the defect stays
  latent for other deployments on small volumes.
- **Option B — default `20`.** Removes the defect for every deployment. Cost: on a large volume
  that is >80% full for unrelated reasons, `_gc_pass` would evict the whole store every pass
  without reaching the target. Bounding how much such a pass evicts needs the store's real
  size — exactly the accounting `itchy-arbored-peccary` restores, so Option B should follow it.

## Testing

Run from the worktree venv (`env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" ...`).

- **RED oracle** — `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py -q`. New cases drive the real
  `janitor.run_gc()` with `free_bytes` injected for a 30-GiB volume (`total` stubbed via
  `shutil.disk_usage`): at 85% used (4.50 GiB free) and at 90% used (3.00 GiB free) the pass
  MUST evict a non-grace entry. Against current code both evict 0 — the observed RED. A
  hysteresis case asserts the pass continues to the 7.5-GiB-free target rather than stopping
  at the 6.0-GiB trigger; a grace case asserts an entry touched inside `grace_seconds` is still
  skipped. A `free_watermark_pct=0` case asserts today's behaviour is unchanged.
- **Exact-defect mutation** — reset the compose/config `free_watermark_pct` to 0 (restoring
  the absolute-only watermark) and re-run the module: the new cases MUST return to RED.
- **Config seam** — `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py -k tunable -q`, covering
  `REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT=20` surviving int resolution (not truncating to 0).
- **Docs pin** — `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_docs.py -q`.
- **No regression** — `pytest tests/unit -q`; `make lint`; `make typecheck`; `make config-check`.
- **Post-deploy (operator, read-only)** — `rebar/host:root_disk_used_percent` shows reclaim
  events with peaks under 85%, where the pre-fix series peaked at 90% (2026-08-17) and 87%
  (2026-08-18).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A faithful local reproduction identifies the dominant disk consumer and the component
      responsible for the 90%→48% reclaim.
- [x] A discriminating runtime experiment proves the root cause and rules out the surviving
      Docker-vs-snapshot alternative.
- [x] A test is observed RED on the proven mechanism, GREEN after repair, then RED again under
      the exact-defect mutation — proved by `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_janitor.py -q`.
- [x] The repaired path reclaims before a 30-GiB root crosses the 85% alarm floor — proved by
      the 4.50-GiB-free case evicting.
- [x] The repaired path reclaims with hysteresis — proved by the hysteresis case asserting
      reclaim continues to the 7.5-GiB-free target, not stopping at the 6.0-GiB trigger.
- [x] Live/grace snapshot entries are preserved — proved by the grace-window case.
- [x] Existing fail-safe deploy/review semantics remain intact — proved by `pytest tests/unit -q`
      green (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` is absent from this ticket's file impact).
- [x] Documentation is updated — proved by `pytest tests/unit/test_snapshot_docs.py -q` green.

Set REBAR_GATE_FREE_WATERMARK_PCT for the review-bot service so the 30-GiB root reclaims below the 85% alarm floor.

Register the new REBAR_GATE_* env vars.
